title: #3. Technology / AI
text:
Technology, especially AI, has changed our lives in a pretty dramatic way.

On the positive side, it has made a lot of tasks much faster and easier. As a programmer, I use AI tools almost every day for writing code, fixing bugs, and looking things up. What used to take hours can now take minutes.

But honestly, that is also what worries me. AI is getting good enough to replace a lot of software jobs. I have actually felt that pressure myself, which is part of why I am planning to shift my career toward electrical engineering. Physical, hands-on work is a lot harder for AI to replace.

Another problem is that people may depend on AI too much. If people always let AI think for them, they may lose their own problem-solving skills. So, I think AI is very useful, but we still need to use it carefully.

title: #5 -> #13. Qualities for Success
text:
I think three qualities are important for success: curiosity, adaptability, and persistence.

First, curiosity helps people keep learning. For example, I started archery and programming because I found them interesting. When I am curious, I can learn without being forced.

Second, adaptability is important because the world changes fast. I worked as a programmer, but when I saw AI changing the industry, I decided to change my direction. It was not easy, but I think flexible people have more chances.

Finally, persistence matters. When I started archery, I could not hit the target well. When I started programming, I was also confused. But I kept practicing, and I improved over time.

So, I believe success is not only about talent. It is about staying curious, adapting to change, and not giving up.

title: #6. Working with Others
text:
Personally, I think working with others tends to produce better results than working alone.

When I work by myself, it's easy to get too comfortable with my own ideas. I might think something is good enough when it actually isn't. Also, other people have different experiences and different ways of thinking. So the final result is usually better.

In addition, I tend to work harder when others are depending on me. When I work alone, I sometimes get too relaxed. But in a group, I naturally push myself more. Also, staying motivated is easier in a group. When things get difficult, seeing others still working hard keeps me going too.

So, I think working with others is usually better because it gives me new ideas and keeps me motivated.

title: #7. Environment
text:
In my opinion, protecting the environment is important, but I think individual actions have limited impact.

Climate change is clearly a real problem. Temperatures are rising and extreme weather is becoming more common. Also, most of this is caused by human activity.

However, I think the real responsibility is on large companies and governments. A large company can create much more pollution than one person. So I think it is unfair to blame only individuals.

That said, I still think individuals should do something. Small habits like saving electricity or buying less can still help. Also, if enough people change their behaviour, it puts pressure on companies to change too.

So in my opinion, protecting the environment matters. But real change has to come from companies and governments.

title: #8. Historical Place in Korea
text:
One historical place that I think is worth mentioning is Hwaseong Fortress in Suwon, South Korea.

It was built in the late 18th Century by King Jeongjo. It was not only built for military defense, but also a symbol of his political vision and his love for his father.

Also, it's a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and I think it deserves that recognition. The walls and gates are still standing, and you can actually walk along them and see the whole city from above.

I actually live near Suwon, so I have been there a few times. To me, it doesn't feel like a typical museum. It feels like a real historical place.

So if someone asked me to recommend a historical place in Korea, Hwaseong Fortress would be my first answer.

title: #9. Money and Happiness
text:
In my opinion, money and happiness are related, but not directly.

Money doesn't buy happiness by itself. However, it removes a lot of stress. For instance, when you are worried about rent or bills, it is very hard to feel happy. So up to a certain point, having more money does improve your life.

For me personally, I feel most comfortable when I have enough financial stability to make my own choices. That sense of control is more important than the actual amount.

Also, I think health and money are connected. Staying healthy saves money in the long run. And having enough money makes it easier to take care of your health. So they affect each other.

In my opinion, money is not the key to happiness, but it does make life a lot easier.

title: #10. Something Special to Me
text:
One thing that is very special to me is my two leopard geckos Lily and Lala.

I got them a few years ago because I was curious about keeping reptiles. At first, I was not sure what to expect. But taking care of them turned out to be more rewarding than I thought.

Also, they each have their own personality, which is a bit surprising for lizards.

For me, what makes them special is the daily routine. Feeding them and maintaining their space gives my day a routine. I did not realize how much I needed that until I had it.

Also, I'm planning to move to Canada soon, and figuring out what happens to them is honestly one of the hardest parts. That made me realize how much I care about them.

So, more than any object or trip, Lily and Lala represent a quiet and stable period of my life. That means a lot to me.

title: #12. Chuseok
text:
One tradition that is very important in Korea is Chuseok, which is basically the Korean harvest festival.

It is celebrated in autumn, usually in September or October. During this time, most Koreans travel back to their hometown to spend time with family. Also, families prepare a lot of traditional food together, especially songpyeon, which is a type of rice cake.

One thing that makes it unique is that families perform a ceremony to honor their ancestors. In my opinion, this is something special about Korean culture. It keeps people connected to their roots.

For me personally, what I enjoy most is the food and the atmosphere. Everyone is off work, the whole country feels quieter, and families are actually together. That does not happen very often in modern life.

So I think Chuseok is not just a holiday. It is one of the few times Koreans genuinely slow down.

title: #14. Indie Game Studio
text:
If I had the chance, I would start a small indie game studio.

I have worked as a developer for a few years, so I understand how games are made. I also know that many talented developers have good ideas, but they often do not have enough money to make their own games.

At first, I would start with a small team, maybe three or four people. A small team is easier to manage, and communication is much simpler.

For the first project, I would not try to make a huge game. Instead, I would focus on making one small but high-quality game. In my opinion, many indie studios fail because they try to do too much too fast.

So, I would start small, make a good game, and grow slowly.

title: Birthday Script - Number Hold
text:
In Korea, birthdays are usually celebrated with family or close friends.

One common tradition is eating seaweed soup. It has a special meaning because mothers often eat it after giving birth. So eating it on a birthday is a way to remember and appreciate your mother.

People also prepare a cake, sing a birthday song, and sometimes give gifts. With family, we usually have dinner together. With friends, we might go to a cafe or a restaurant.

One birthday I remember was a quiet one with my family. It was not a big party, but we ate good food, talked together, and had cake. What made it special was the feeling that people cared about me.

So, I think birthdays are not only about gifts or parties. They are about spending time with people who remember you.
